about: Every input the BBC Micro's two models are measured from: where it came from, who made it, its licence as stated where it was found (null when none is stated), when it was fetched, and its size and SHA-256. The tools never fetch: each input is fetched by hand into the folder BBC_MODEL_INPUTS names, under `file`, and the tools refuse a file whose SHA-256 is not the one here. `width` and `height` are the pixels as stored (null for a file that is not an image). `committed` names the resized copy in site/src/assets/photos/ when there is one; a scan, or an input with no stated licence, is never committed. The ids are those of docs/bbc-micro/facts/models.md.

sources.author: Daniel Beardsmore
sources.use: The top of the case from above: the keys registered to K1 by a homography on the key plane, the case's front edge, and later the recess, LEDs, badge strip and grille; task 8: the case top registered on its four corners to the Service Manual's 415 by 345 mm, the keyboard's opening, the badge strip and the three lights, and the keys' colours. Fetched again on 13 October 2026 from Commons; its SHA-1 was Commons' (f8ee3ba32bb3ea9c107a34e64282caca21c533e8) and its SHA-256 the one above

sources.author: Stuart Brady (assumed by Commons)
sources.use: The rear: the ports' heights and labels; task 8: the rear ports' places and heights, the vents and the mains panel, on the scale of the 15-way D shell. sources.author: 8BS
sources.use: A populated Issue 7 board: the chips' markings, registered to I1 by homography. Stored 2048 by 1536 with EXIF orientation 8, so shown upright as 1536 by 2048. Task 4 registers it, in its pixels as stored (which lie as I1 does, rear connectors at the top), to the board frame on chip pins marked by hand, and compares the component side's copper with it

sources.author: Dominic Beesley
sources.use: Every key centre on the BBC layout, read from each switch footprint's 4 mm centre hole: the frame the photographs of the keyboard are registered to, and the keys' places and sizes in the outside model (task 8). Dominic Beesley's repository github.com/dominicbeesley/bbc-keyboard, read from its fork in the dbhq-uk organisation (AGENTS.md rule 3) at commit 5ec53df566c77424caa6be827d0831da3916ecfa: fetched on 13 October 2026 with `gh api -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw" repos/dbhq-uk/bbc-keyboard/contents/KiCad/bbc-keyboard/bbc-keyboard.kicad_pcb?ref=5ec53df566c77424caa6be827d0831da3916ecfa`, whose git blob SHA-1 (c1bfd4788faa4a5930b21c519c6748f2c61c4bad) is the one the fork's API gives, and whose SHA-256 is the one task 0 recorded on 4 October 2026 from a clone of the original. The LICENSE at that commit in the fork is the MIT notice kept in data/README.md
